selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main claim of the Fifth Truth about the universe?
questions.answer: The universe shows that its Maker and Manager is one and has no partner.

questions.question: Besides order, what other quality is paired with it in the passage?
questions.answer: Regularity.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both the whole cosmos and its smaller parts?
questions.answer: To show that the same truth appears in the largest and smallest levels.

questions.question: Why is it important that many things are similar in nature and found in many places?
questions.answer: That sameness points to one source managing them all, not many separate rulers.

questions.question: How is the world’s administration described through the picture of a palace?
questions.answer: It is shown as carefully built, decorated, and maintained by one master.

questions.question: What would “neither like nor peer” mean in simple language?
questions.answer: No one is similar to Him in His rule and no one matches Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Creator’s need for helpers?
questions.answer: It says He has no helper, assistant, equal, or partner.

questions.question: How does the passage connect unity with peace in management?
questions.answer: It shows that one ruler brings harmony, while many rulers would bring conflict.

questions.question: What character trait should a believing student build from reading this passage?
questions.answer: Strong certainty in tawhid and thoughtful reflection on creation.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the traveller notice at the second stage?
questions.answer: He notices the perfect order and regularity in the whole universe and in everything inside it.

questions.question: Name two kinds of signs in creation that the passage points to.
questions.answer: The careful order of the universe and the widespread presence of the same elements and species.

questions.question: Why does the passage repeat the idea of “the same” in different places?
questions.answer: To stress that one pattern and one rule are operating throughout creation.

questions.question: What is the significance of the earth being covered by the same elements and kinds of creatures in many places?
questions.answer: It shows that one power spreads, manages, and sustains them everywhere.

questions.question: What does the spread of the same elements across the earth suggest about control?
questions.answer: It suggests one power controls and uses them everywhere.

questions.question: What are some things the passage denies about Allah?
questions.answer: It denies that He has an equal, partner, assistant, opposite, weakness, or deficiency.

questions.question: Why would assigning partners to Allah go against what the passage describes?
questions.answer: Because the passage describes a united, well-run order, while partners would cause disagreement and division.

questions.question: How should a reader classify the proof given here: mainly emotional, mainly visual, or mainly reason-based?
questions.answer: It is mainly reason-based, using signs in creation to reach a conclusion.

questions.question: Is the proof in this passage presented as hidden and hard to see, or as obvious and direct?
questions.answer: It is presented as obvious and direct.

questions.question: What quality of the cosmos is mentioned first in the Fifth Truth?
questions.answer: Its complete and beautiful order.

questions.question: What about the universe makes it a witness to Allah’s oneness in this passage?
questions.answer: Its perfect arrangement, regular operation, and unified system make it a witness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Divine Names and deeds at work in the world?
questions.answer: They reach across all things or most things and work everywhere in a wide, complete way.

questions.question: What do the Divine Names and deeds do in this passage?
questions.answer: They encompass creation broadly and act throughout it.

questions.question: What is the role of regularity in the argument of this passage?
questions.answer: Regularity is evidence that creation is directed wisely and not left to many competing powers.

questions.question: Why does the passage say partners cannot fit into this system?
questions.answer: Because partners would bring conflict and disorder, while the world shows harmony and steady order.
